business_model.claim: Servicing fee revenue is driven by changes in market valuations, client activity and asset flows, net new business, and pricing; over five years, market valuations impacted servicing fees by approximately 3% on average, client activity and flows by approximately (1)%, net new business by approximately 1%, and pricing pressure by approximately (2)% annually.
quotes: Generally, our servicing fee revenues are affected by several factors, including changes in market valuations, client activity and asset flows, net new business and the manner in which we price our services.

Over the five years ended December 31, 2025, we estimate that worldwide equity and fixed income market valuations impacted our servicing fees revenue by approximately 3% on average with a range of (4)% to 8% annually
Over the five years ended December 31, 2025, we estimate that client activity and asset flows, together, impacted our servicing fees revenue by approximately (1)% on average
Over the five years ended December 31, 2025, net new business, which includes business both won and lost, has affected our servicing fee revenues by approximately 1% on average
On average, over the five years ended December 31, 2025, we estimate that pricing pressure with respect to existing clients has impacted our servicing fees by approximately (2)% annually

quotes: On August 12, 2026, State Street Corporation ("State Street") issued and sold 500,000 depositary shares (the "Depositary Shares") each representing a 1/100th ownership interest in a share of State Street's Fixed Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series L, without par value per share (the "Series L Preferred Stock"), with a liquidation preference of $100,000 per share (equivalent to $1,000 per Depositary Share) in a public offering pursuant to a registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-288196) and a related prospectus supplement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC").
State Street expects to receive net proceeds from the offering of the Depositary Shares of approximately $495.7 million, after deducting the underwriting discount and estimated offering expenses.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (8-K Item 5.02)
material_events.claim: State Street announced on September 14, 2026 that Ann Fogarty was appointed Enterprise Chief Operating Officer (succeeding Mostapha Tahiri) and Mostapha Tahiri was appointed President of State Street Alpha, effective immediately.
quotes: On September 14, 2026, State Street Corporation announced two executive leadership appointments. Mostapha Tahiri, currently Enterprise Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed President of State Street Alpha and will continue as Chairman of Asia Pacific. Ann Fogarty, currently Investment Services Chief Operating Officer, has been appointed Enterprise Chief Operating Officer, succeeding Mr. Tahiri. These appointments are effective immediately.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor) and quantified in P3 (MD&A pricing discussion); the (2)–(3)% annual drag is management's own estimate.
risks.claim: Sustained pricing pressure in custodial and investment management services erodes fee revenue growth and operating margins.
quotes: We have also experienced, and anticipate that we will continue to experience, significant pricing pressure in many of our core businesses, particularly our custodial and investment management services.

On average, over the five years ended December 31, 2025, we estimate that pricing pressure with respect to existing clients has impacted our servicing fees by approximately (2)% annually, with the impact ranging from (2)% to (3)% in any given year and approximately (2)% and (3)% in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor) and P3 (MD&A); the 10 bps NIM decline in 2025 is a concrete data point showing the mechanism at work.
risks.claim: Declines in prevailing interest rates could reduce net interest income and force portfolio management decisions that lower capital or liquidity ratios.
quotes: changes in prevailing interest rates or other market conditions have led, and were they to occur in the future could further lead, to decreases in our NII or to portfolio management decisions resulting in reductions in our capital or liquidity ratios
NII increased 1% compared to 2024, primarily driven by 11% growth in average interest-earnings assets, partially offset by a 10 bps decline in NIM.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor with specific percentages); F1 provides the current balance-sheet composition.
risks.claim: The investment securities portfolio, at approximately 29% of total assets, exposes the company to mark-to-market losses and capital ratio deterioration from adverse rate or credit events.
quotes: Our investment securities portfolio represented approximately 29% of our total assets as of December 31, 2025.

The gross interest income associated with our investment portfolio represented approximately 17% of our total gross revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 and has represented as much as 31% of our total gross revenue in the fiscal years since 2007.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor); the short-notice contract term is explicitly called out. Counter-evidence from P5 growth metrics.
risks.claim: Loss or in-sourcing by even one large institutional client could materially reduce AUC/A or AUM and fee revenue in the affected period.
quotes: the loss or gain of one client, or even a portion of the assets controlled by one client, or a client's decision to in-source certain services that we provide, could have a significant effect on our AUC/A or our AUM, as applicable, in the relevant period.
Many of our core services are subject to contracts that have relatively short terms or may be terminated by our client after a short notice period.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (Business section, G-SIB discussion) and P3 (Capital section with specific ratios and target ranges).
risks.claim: As a G-SIB, State Street faces enhanced capital, liquidity and conduct requirements that raise costs and restrict activities relative to non-G-SIB competitors.
quotes: As a G-SIB, we are subject to extensive regulation and supervision with respect to our operations and activities. Not all of our competitors have similarly been designated as systemically important nor are all of them subject to the same degree of regulation as a bank or financial holding company; therefore some of our competitors may not be subject to the same limitations, requirements and standards with respect to their operations and activities.

Our CET1 capital ratio was 11.6% as of December 31, 2025, compared to 10.9% as of December 31, 2024, primarily due to capital generated from earnings, partially offset by continued capital return. Our Tier 1 leverage ratio increased to 5.5% as of December 31, 2025, compared to 5.2% as of December 31, 2024.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factor); counter-evidence from P5 (3Q26 software services metrics and Wealth Services mandate win).
risks.claim: Adoption of AI, distributed ledger technology and related regulatory frameworks by competitors or new entrants could materially disrupt State Street's servicing and investment management franchises.
quotes: the adoption and implementation of evolving and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and distributed ledger technology, and related regulatory frameworks, have the potential to disrupt materially the activities of the financial services industry, the operation of financial markets, processes, infrastructure and service providers, including State Street, and the servicing and other requirements of financial services clients, including our clients.

new market entrants and competitors may address or influence changes in the markets more rapidly than we do, may have materially greater resources to invest in infrastructure, technology and product development than we do, or may provide clients with a more attractive or cost-efficient offering of products and services, adversely affecting our business.

thesis_change.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, filed 2026-02-23); no post-2026-10-31 evidence contradicts or updates it
thesis_change.claim: The $2.50 trillion AUC/A installation pipeline and its expected 70% 2026 / balance 2027 conversion timeline remain as previously stated; no evidence effective after 2026-10-31 alters the schedule or the onboarding-risk caveat.
quotes: With respect to the current asset mandates of approximately $2.5 trillion of AUC/A that are yet to be installed as of December 31, 2025, we expect the conversion will mostly occur over the coming 24 months, with approximately 70% expected to be installed in 2026, with the balance expected to be installed largely in 2027.

thesis_change.basis: stated in P3 (10-K), P4 (10-Q MD&A), and F2 (10-Q income statement); no post-2026-10-31 evidence changes these figures
thesis_change.claim: AUM growth as a second revenue engine remains as described: AUM rose 20% in 2025 to $5.67 trillion and reached $6.31 trillion by Sep 2026, with management fee revenue up 13% in 2025; the dependence on net inflows and supportive market levels in passive equity and fixed-income products is unaltered.
quotes: AUM of $5.67 trillion as of December 31, 2025 increased 20% compared to December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher market levels and net inflows.
As of September 30, 2026, we reported $59.17 trillion in AUC/A and $6.31 trillion in AUM.
Management fees increased 13% in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to higher average market levels and net inflows.

thesis_change.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P2 (10-K Risk Factors); no post-2026-10-31 evidence changes the G-SIB status or cost differential
thesis_change.claim: As a G-SIB, State Street faces enhanced regulatory capital, liquidity and stress-testing requirements that impose costs not borne by most competitors, and management states peers have 'substantially greater financial resources' to absorb these costs; no newer evidence alters this regulatory positioning.

Not all of our competitors have similarly been designated as systemically important nor are all of them subject to the same degree of regulation as a bank or financial holding company; therefore some of our competitors may not be subject to the same limitations, requirements and standards with respect to their operations and activities. Most other financial institutions designated as systemically important have substantially greater financial resources and a broader base of operations than we do and are, consequently, in a better competitive position to manage and bear the costs of this enhanced regulatory requirement.
